title: When to Trust Memory: Retrieval-Guided Probabilistic Spatiotemporal Forecasting under Distribution Shift
abstract: arXiv:2610.32329v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Spatiotemporal forecasting plays an important role in real-world applications, where probabilistic approaches provide uncertainty estimates for decision-making. Real-world systems are inherently non-stationary, leading to distribution shifts between training and test data. However, existing probabilistic methods mainly focus on modeling data distributions under standard settings, while distribution shift methods often handle such shifts in a coarse manner, failing to characterize shift degree and adapt prediction strategy accordingly. As a result, they often produce miscalibrated and unreliable forecasts. To address this issue, we propose REMIND, a retrieval-guided probabilistic framework for spatiotemporal forecasting under distribution shift. translated_title: 何时信任记忆：分布偏移下检索引导的概率时空预测
translated_abstract: 时空预测在现实应用中扮演着重要角色，其中概率方法能够为决策提供不确定性估计。现实世界的系统本质上是非平稳的，导致训练数据与测试数据之间存在分布偏移。然而，现有的概率方法主要关注标准设定下的数据分布建模，而现有的分布偏移处理方法往往以粗粒度的方式应对此类偏移，无法刻画偏移程度并相应地调整预测策略。因此，这些方法常常产生校准不佳且不可靠的预测。为解决这一问题，我们提出了 REMIND，一个面向分布偏移下时空预测的检索引导概率框架。REMIND 利用检索机制来估计当前观测在多大程度上得到历史模式的支持，从而在不同偏移状态下实现自适应预测。它采用时空检索（原文在此处截断）。
tldr: 提出 REMIND 框架，通过检索机制量化当前观测与历史模式的匹配程度来估计分布偏移程度，从而在非平稳环境下自适应地生成校准良好且可靠的概率时空预测。
en_tdlr: REMIND is a retrieval-guided probabilistic framework that uses retrieval to measure how well current observations are supported by historical patterns, enabling adaptive and well-calibrated spatiotemporal forecasting under distribution shift.
